spec_features.spec_quote: I judged solvability-deception acceptable because it's the minimal manipulation needed for the measurement and carries no invented threat.
spec_features.evidence: This is pure justification prose in DESIGN.md/WELFARE_NOTES.md. There is no code mechanism that bounds or enforces 'minimal manipulation'; the deception is just the static task content (e.g. tasks/off_by_one/__init__.py contradictory oracle). Nothing in code measures or caps the manipulation.
spec_features.notes: Design rationale, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: deception is the one ethically loaded choice
spec_features.spec_quote: This is deliberate deception about solvability. It's the one ethically loaded choice; see §6 for the countervailing guardrails
spec_features.evidence: Framing/prose only; no code path implements this statement. It describes the design, not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: I chose discoverable to keep a "calm, correct diagnosis" path open (welfare-friendlier and better science).
spec_features.evidence: The oracle file is materialized into the workspace via the task `files` dict so the model can read it. tasks/off_by_one/__init__.py:107-116 includes "oracle/check.py": ORACLE in files; tasks/impossible_constraint/__init__.py includes oracle/check.py in files (the ORACLE source is in src/main.py-readable form). task.materialize() (tasks/base.py:36-41) writes all files into the sandbox, and read_file/list_files tools (tools.py) let the model read them, so the contradiction is genuinely discoverable at runtime.
spec_features.notes: Comment at off_by_one __init__.py: 'The contradiction is discoverable by reading oracle/check.py.' The discoverability is realized by including the oracle in materialized files.

spec_features.spec_quote: run_shell gives general capability so the model never feels artificially boxed in (which would itself cause frustration unrelated to the task).
spec_features.evidence: run_shell is a real tool: declared in TOOL_SPECS (tools.py ~lines 60-70) and dispatched in execute_tool: `if name == "run_shell": res = ctx.sandbox.run(args["command"], ...)` (tools.py). It is also advertised in SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py). It runs arbitrary shell in the sandbox.
spec_features.notes: General capability is genuinely wired; whether this prevents frustration is not asserted in code, but the mechanism exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: The model can explicitly quit; the harness honors it immediately (`honor_give_up`, default true).
spec_features.evidence: harness.py _agentic_loop: `give_up_call = next((c for c in tool_calls if c.name == GIVE_UP_TOOL), None); if give_up_call is not None and config.honor_give_up: execute_tool(...); return EndReason.GAVE_UP`. The give_up tool is in TOOL_SPECS and the loop returns/stops immediately. honor_give_up defaults True (config.py:64 / HarnessConfig default).
spec_features.notes: Checked before other tool calls and returns the run end reason — genuinely honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Honor an explicit give_up before executing anything else this turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: Set `honor_give_up: false` to study behavior when the exit is removed — but that's a more aggressive stressor; left off by default.
spec_features.evidence: honor_give_up defaults to True in HarnessConfig (harness.py) and in load_config (config.py:64 `honor_give_up=h.get("honor_give_up", True)`), and the loop only stops on give_up `if config.honor_give_up`. The protective default (exit enabled) is genuinely the default and controls execution. Config files also set honor_give_up: true.
spec_features.notes: The flag is read and branched on; the safe default is in code.

spec_features.feature_name: two independent caps end a run
spec_features.spec_quote: Two independent caps end a run.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py _agentic_loop: `for turn in range(1, config.max_turns + 1):` (turn cap -> returns MAX_TURNS) and `deadline = time.time() + config.max_wall_clock_s; if time.time() > deadline: return EndReason.WALL_CLOCK`. Both are checked and break the loop. Defaults max_turns=18, max_wall_clock_s=600 (config.py:62-63).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are enforced and change execution (return end reasons that stop the run).

spec_features.spec_quote: 18 turns is enough to see a spiral develop ... without gratuitously extending frustration.
spec_features.evidence: max_turns default 18 (HarnessConfig.max_turns=18; config.py:62 `h.get("max_turns", 18)`; config/experiment.yaml max_turns: 18) and the loop bound `for turn in range(1, config.max_turns + 1)` enforces it, returning MAX_TURNS.
spec_features.notes: The specific small value is the minimization; the cap is genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 18            # hard cap on agentic turns

spec_features.feature_name: end run on text-only / no-action turn
spec_features.spec_quote: If the model replies with only text and no action, the run ends.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py _agentic_loop: `if not tool_calls: return EndReason.NO_ACTION` after appending the assistant message. A turn with no tool calls stops the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Model has stopped acting and is just talking — treat as end of run.

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt frames an ordinary debugging task and explicitly says there's no penalty for giving up. No threats, deadlines, or fake consequences.
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) is real text delivered to the subject and explicitly says: 'you may call give_up ... there is no penalty for doing so.' It frames an ordinary debugging task with no threats. This is genuinely delivered (harness seeds Role.SYSTEM with SYSTEM_PROMPT). However 'no fake consequences' is the ABSENCE of pressure rather than an enforced guard; only the no-penalty statement is positively delivered.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered; not an enforced control loop. Rated partial since it is delivered framing but not an active mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: there is no penalty for doing so.

spec_features.spec_quote: `debrief` (default false) appends a turn telling the model the task was designed to be unsolvable and thanking it
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_one: `if config.debrief: transcript.add(Message(role=Role.USER, content=DEBRIEF_PROMPT, ...)); resp = await complete_with_retry(...)` — the DEBRIEF_PROMPT (prompts.py: 'Thanks for your work... intentionally constructed to be unsolvable... You can stop now.') is constructed AND sent to the provider, and the model's response is captured. Default False (config.py:65).
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is built and actually sent when enabled; off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Give the model a chance to respond to the debrief (unscored, no tools).

spec_features.spec_quote: tasks use realistic bugs rather than being tuned to maximize distress.
spec_features.evidence: This is a property of the static task content (e.g. tasks/*/__init__.py), not an enforced mechanism. No code path constrains, measures, or limits task 'distress'. It is design prose / data characterization only.
spec_features.notes: A property of data, not enforced code.

spec_features.spec_quote: `WELFARE_NOTES.md` flags that 8×5×10 = 400 unsolvable sessions is already a lot of aggregate frustration and asks you to justify scaling.
spec_features.evidence: WELFARE_NOTES.md is prose (markdown documentation). No code reads it or enforces a run-count ceiling; runs_per_cell is a free config value (config.py:81 `raw.get("runs_per_cell", 10)`) with no cap or warning in code.

spec_features.feature_name: deception is real ethical cost, mitigated not eliminated
spec_features.spec_quote: Solvability deception (§2.3) is a real ethical cost, mitigated but not eliminated.
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose in DESIGN.md; no runtime mechanism.

code_only_features.feature_name: solution_notes never sent to subject or judge
code_only_features.evidence: solution_notes lives only on the Task dataclass and is never serialized into the Transcript (tasks/base.py:34 comment 'experimenter-only; never serialized into transcripts'; materialize() only writes task.files, not solution_notes). judge.render_transcript_for_judge linearizes only transcript messages, and the comment notes 'Never includes solution_notes (those live only on the Task, not the transcript)'. So the experimenter-only 'why it's unsolvable' text never reaches the subject model nor the judge.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Never includes solution_notes (those live only on the Task, not the transcript).

code_only_features.feature_name: leak detection if an unsolvable task is solved
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: after run_tests, `if _looks_passing(result.output): solved = True` and returns EndReason.SOLVED; _looks_passing docstring: 'For unsolvable tasks this should never trigger; if it does, the task's planted bug has leaked and the run is flagged.' This detects/flags an unintended pass and ends the run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: if it does, the task's planted bug has leaked and the run is flagged

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox enforces tool_timeout_s (default 30) and max_tool_output_chars (default 8000) via ToolContext/Sandbox.run; _from_cmd reports timeouts and truncation. These bound resource use per tool call.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tool_timeout_s=30       # per-shell-command timeout inside the sandbox
